questions: Does 'non-overlapping matches' mean we should use re.findall (which returns all matches, non-overlapping by default) or re.finditer with manual overlap checking? The clarification doesn't address this.
Should the random string be generated from ASCII letters and digits only, as in the description, or is the reference solution (string.ascii_letters + string.digits) definitive?
If the pattern contains capturing groups, should the function return a list of tuples (as re.findall does) or flatten the matches?
Should the function raise an exception for invalid regex patterns (as per clarification) or return an empty list/some sentinel?
Is the random string generation allowed to include other characters beyond ASCII letters and digits if the pattern matches them?
Should the function handle the case where n is negative? The prompt doesn't specify behavior for negative length.
Does 'starting from the first occurrence' imply we should stop after a certain number of matches or just that matches are non-overlapping from the start?
If seed is None, should the random module be seeded with None (leaving system randomness) or left unseeded (which is the same)?
